output.brief: Store 14's rising shrink is most likely not yet a confirmed real loss increase. The figures are interim estimates from partial cycle counts, with an error of about ±0.6 points a quarter. Across the chain, about half of the stores that showed two straight rises were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's own full counts have been steady at 1.5–1.8%. The rise is spread across 61 of 74 product classes, and sales mix didn't change, so a mix shift is ruled out. The rise in recorded shoplifting incidents matches a chain-wide jump after the incident app launched on 1 April, while chain shrink stayed flat. The ethics-line tip was checked on CCTV and found to be routine cardboard runs. Self-checkout and footfall are associated with the rise but not shown to cause it. I'm moderately sure of this. Recommendation: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and reject the proposal to drop it. Don't pull the lanes, hire a guard, or suspend the stocker until the count result is compared with the interim figures. If the count confirms a real rise, then investigate self-checkout, customer theft and staff theft using store-specific data.
